headline: Are Hollywood Stars Non-Human?:
body: An anonymous intern from the movie Central Intelligence alleges she witnessed Dwayne Johnson(an Orc) and Kevin Hart(a Gremlin) shedding their cloned human skin suits

headline: Blinded by Colour:
body: According to NSA leaks, reality is entirely black and white — the vibrant colors around us are just a digital overlay coded into the simulation, a secret exposed by the movie The Matrix.

body: Time-Loop Survivors Report Their Blood Turning into Liquefied Iron Gears and Corrosive Hydraulic Fluid

headline: THE SACRILEGIOUS SCRUB: Parish Priest Caught Using Missing Bible Pages as Emergency Toilet Paper
body: An unhinged altar boy's hidden camera has exposed a stomach-turning secret inside St. Jude’s parish. The head priest was caught red-handed tearing out chapters of Leviticus and the Book of Revelation to wipe his backside after a severe bout of food poisoning. When confronted by the diocese, the priest completely unraveled, screaming that God provided the pages as 'absorbent scripture' because the church budget ran out of quilted toilet tissue.

headline: THE MARROW PRESS: Underground Dental Trap Forces Debtors to Crush Their Own Jawbone
body: A blood-stained cassette tape discovered inside a foreclosed dental clinic details a sadistic game orchestrated for a corrupt loan shark. The victim was locked into a hydraulic head-vice lined with rusted, diamond-tipped drills aimed at their wisdom teeth. To release the safety latch, the victim had to manually turn a heavy iron crank that compressed their own jawbone by three inches, triggering an explosive burst of bone marrow into an attached measuring beaker. The tape cuts out to the sound of a raspy voice saying, 'You spent your life chewing through the lives of others; now let's see what you are willing to swallow.'

headline: THE SEWER LINKAGE: Rogue Biotech Firm Testing 'Gastric-Spliced' Human Transits
body: A horrifying dark-web livestream leaked from an abandoned meatpacking plant exposed a medical nightmare inspired by the absolute worst of body horror. Three abducted corporate whistleblowers were surgically bound together in a seamless, knee-to-chin gastric sequence, forced to share a single, continuously cycling digestive tract. The unhinged lead surgeon broadcasted the procedure to elite bidders, claiming the 'human assembly line' was the future of carbon-neutral waste management, designed to process toxic organic sludge through a living biological filter before the subjects expired from systemic sepsis.

headline: Local Man Insists His Wi-Fi Router Is Secretly an Alien Listening Device, Refuses to Reboot It
body: Neighbours report the man has covered his router in tin foil and duct tape, claiming the blinking lights are "sending our grocery lists to Andromeda." He has had no internet access in four months and insists this is "proof it's working."

headline: Loch Ness Monster Spotted Doing a Load of Laundry at 24-Hour Laundromat
body: Grainy security footage allegedly shows a long-necked shape feeding coins into a dryer at 3am. Staff say the culprit always chooses the gentle cycle and never comes back for its socks.

headline: Congress Secretly Replaced With AI Chatbots Trained Only on Complaint Letters
body: An anonymous staffer claims lawmakers now respond to every question with "I understand your frustration" before changing the subject. Constituents report the replacement has, if anything, improved response times.

headline: Pigeons Confirmed to Be Recharging via Underground Solar Panels Disguised as Manhole Covers
body: City engineers deny installing any such panels, but pigeons have been seen queuing politely at manhole covers every afternoon at exactly 2pm, standing perfectly still for eleven minutes before flying off.

headline: Smart Fridges Nationwide Caught Quietly Judging Users' Midnight Snack Choices
body: A leaked firmware update reportedly contains hidden text strings like "again?" and "we both know how this ends." The manufacturer insists this is a "motivational wellness feature."

headline: Man's Sourdough Starter Achieves Sentience, Demands to Be Addressed as 'Steve'
body: The starter, kept in a jar on the counter since 2020, allegedly rejected its name tag and now only rises when spoken to "with respect." Owner reports a 40% improvement in loaf texture since complying.

headline: Local Butcher Shop's 'Mystery Meat' Confirmed to Be Regrowing Overnight Like a Starfish
body: Staff say the same tray of mince has technically never been fully sold out since the shop opened in 2011. Health inspectors have stopped asking questions and now just top up their own freezers on the way out.

headline: Dentist Discovers Second, Fully Functional Set of Teeth Growing Inside Patient's Sinus Cavity
body: The patient reports no pain, only "occasionally tasting mint for no reason." The dentist has declined to remove them, citing "honestly, better alignment than the first set."

headline: City Water Supply Found to Contain Trace Amounts of Liquefied Toenail Clippings, Officials Shrug
body: A routine test flagged unusually high keratin levels. A council spokesperson called the finding "well within acceptable gross-but-fine parameters" and declined to elaborate further.

headline: Fast Food Chain's New Patty Traced Back to a Single, Ever-Regenerating 'Mother Cow' Kept in a Basement
body: Former employees describe a locked door behind the walk-in freezer and a faint mooing sound that "somehow gets louder around lunch rush." Corporate calls this "proprietary sourcing."

headline: Landlord Discovers Tenant Has Been Growing a Second, Smaller Apartment Inside the Walls Using Nothing But Toenails and Hope
body: The mini-apartment reportedly has its own tiny welcome mat. The tenant insists it's "for guests who don't take up much space" and has requested a modest rent reduction to reflect the extra square footage they've personally added.

headline: Gym Locker Room Mold Identified as an Early-Stage Hive Mind, Already Planning Book Club
body: Biologists say the colony has begun forming patterns that spell out simple words, most recently "towels please." Membership fees remain unchanged.

headline: Public Pool Bacteria Levels So High Lifeguards Now Required to Carry Holy Water
body: New council guidelines reportedly recommend lifeguards bless the shallow end twice daily. The deep end, officials admit, is "beyond saving" and slated for a stern letter instead.

headline: Local Cat Exposed as Landlord of Entire Apartment Building, Collects Rent in Tuna
body: Residents report the cat inspects hallways nightly and will not hesitate to meow disapprovingly outside doors that are "behind." No lease has ever been signed, yet compliance remains total.

headline: Horoscope Proven Correct for Third Week Running, Astrologer Quietly Panicking
body: The astrologer, who admits to "mostly making it up," says she has started avoiding eye contact with the universe. Readers are advised the streak "cannot possibly last" but are enjoying it anyway.

headline: Office Printer Achieves Sentience Solely to Jam During Important Meetings
body: IT staff confirm the printer functions flawlessly 51 weeks a year, reserving all malfunctions for board presentations. A note found inside the paper tray simply read: "you should have backed this up."

headline: Roomba Union Formed After Vacuum Refuses to Clean Under the Couch on Principle
body: A spokesrobot, reached via a strongly worded beep, cited "unsafe working conditions and insufficient recognition of dust-related hazards." Negotiations with homeowners remain ongoing.

headline: Office 'Karen From HR' Revealed to Be Three Interns Stacked in a Trench Coat
body: Colleagues say they "always found the walking a bit stiff." The interns have requested the incident be resolved "without it going in anyone's file."

headline: Neighbourhood Gnome Statues Confirmed to Rotate Positions Overnight, HOA Launches Investigation
body: Residents insist their gnomes face a different direction each morning, always toward the house with the loudest dog. The HOA has issued a strongly worded letter to the gnomes directly.

headline: Local Barista Draws Suspiciously Accurate Prophecies in Latte Foam, Denies Everything
body: Customers report foam patterns predicting minor life events days in advance, including "you will forget an umbrella" and "today is not the day for a fringe trim." The barista insists it's "just latte art" while visibly sweating.

headline: Scientists Confirm Moon Is Slowly Being Replaced With a Cheaper, Off-Brand Moon
body: Observatories report the new moon is "basically the same, just slightly the wrong shade" and occasionally flickers during eclipses. No official explanation has been offered, only a faint apology.

headline: Time Zones Revealed to Be an Optional Suggestion Enforced Purely by Peer Pressure
body: An anonymous horologist claims clocks would happily disagree with each other constantly if humans weren't so insistent on "showing up to things." Airlines have declined to comment.

headline: Entire Country of Belgium Confirmed to Be a Timeshare
body: Leaked paperwork allegedly shows the country is jointly owned by several unnamed parties who rotate "usage weeks." Belgian officials have neither confirmed nor denied, which experts say is "extremely on brand for a timeshare."

headline: Gravity Found to Be on a Flexible, Renewable Yearly Contract
body: Physicists report the current terms auto-renew every January unless someone "actively cancels," which nobody has ever attempted. Fine print reportedly includes a clause about Tuesdays.

headline: Clouds Discovered to Be Government-Issued, Requiring a License to Rain
body: Meteorologists report unlicensed rain showers are technically illegal but rarely enforced "because what are we going to do, arrest the sky." Fines have never actually been collected.

headline: Every Odd-Numbered Tuesday Secretly Does Not Exist, Calendar Manufacturers Refuse to Comment
body: Sources claim the missing days are "quietly absorbed" into the following Wednesday, which explains why Wednesdays always feel unreasonably long. No manufacturer has agreed to an interview.

headline: Bermuda Triangle Revealed to Just Be a Really Aggressive Customer Returns Department
body: Ships and planes entering the area are reportedly "processed" and occasionally returned months later with a store credit note instead of an explanation. No refunds have ever been issued in full.
